findings.title: T-08: maxAttempts=1 が tasks-complete を含む混在 follow-up 違反に影響する
findings.rationale: implementer.ts が現在 tasks-complete (policy follow-up) を outputContracts() で返すことを確認済み（実コード行 258〜263）。step-context-builder.ts (行 135) の maxAttempts は単一値で全 follow-up contracts に適用されるため、T-08 が unpushable-path 含む場合に maxAttempts=1 とすると、同一 step の tasks-complete も 1 回に制限される（従来は 2 回）。T-08 の「他 kind の挙動を変えないこと」は unpushable-path が含まれない場合の保証（TC-034）であり、混在ケースの挙動は仕様化されていない。実装時に TSDoc コメントでこのトレードオフを明記することで対処可能。

findings.title: TC-030 WHEN 句の buildOutputFollowUpPrompt 呼び出しシグネチャ不整合

observations.title: D4: collectPublishablePaths の fail-open 設計は意図的トレードオフ
observations.rationale: T-02 は git コマンド失敗時に例外を投げず取得できた分だけ返す設計を指定している。これにより git status 障害時は Layer 1 の検出が不完全になるが、Layer 2 も同じ collectPublishablePaths を使うため Layer 2 も同様に不完全になる。両層ともに障害時は従来通り remote push 拒否にデグレードする設計（fail-open）であり、設計 D2 で明示的に認識・文書化されている。

findings.title: parseUnpushablePathsFromError creates fragile string-coupling between error factory and halt factory
findings.rationale: executor.ts extracts blocked paths by parsing the error message string with a regex (/protected path\(s\): (.+?)\. Environment/). The error factory and parser must stay byte-for-byte synchronized; no unit test verifies the round-trip. Any message rewording silently returns [] from the parser, causing makeUnpushablePathHalt to receive an empty matchedPaths list. The operator's issue comment then lists zero blocked paths, removing all actionability from the escalation. Paths containing ', ' (comma-space) would also be mis-split. Fix: embed matchedPaths as a typed property on the error object (e.g. class UnpushablePathBlockedError extends SpecRunnerError) so executor.ts reads finalizeErr.matchedPaths directly.

findings.title: commitScopedPaths (round-artifact commit path) lacks Layer 2 backstop — Open Question left unresolved
findings.rationale: Design D7 and T-10 both flag the Open Question: if commitRoundArtifacts does not share commitAndPush, add the same check there. The call graph confirms commitScopedPaths is separate. The final implementation omits the check. Any coordinator step (custom reviewer) whose declared output includes a .github/workflows/** path bypasses both Layer 1 (implementer-only) and Layer 2 (commitAndPush-only), reaching the remote and receiving the historical 'refusing to allow' rejection — defeating the feature for that path.

findings.title: maxAttempts=1 global cap silently reduces tasks-complete repair opportunities for ALL implementer runs on GitHub Actions
findings.rationale: The existing implicit invariant is: implementer always gets OUTPUT_FOLLOWUP_MAX_ATTEMPTS=2 follow-up attempts for tasks-complete. This PR sets maxAttempts=1 for the entire step whenever unpushable-path appears in follow-up contracts. Because implementer.outputContracts() unconditionally adds the unpushable-path contract when pushCapability.patterns.length > 0 (regardless of whether the change touches workflow files), every implementer run on GitHub Actions is affected. A two-unchecked-task scenario that would succeed with two repair attempts now fails after one. The behavioral regression applies to all Actions jobs, not only those that modify workflow files. Fix: use per-contract attempt tracking instead of a scalar maxAttempts, or gate the unpushable-path section in buildPrompt to only appear in attempt 0 so subsequent attempts treat it as resolved.

observations.title: TC-026 test name vs --no-renames implementation: T-02 spec says to extract rename notation but implementation uses --no-renames
observations.rationale: T-02 says rename notation (R old -> new) should yield both paths. The implementation uses --no-renames so renames become D+A entries. TC-026 correctly adapts the test and includes an explanatory comment, so runtime behavior is correct. Only the task-spec language is misleading; no runtime impact.

observations.title: buildOutputFollowUpPrompt footer 'commit and push your changes' is incorrect for implementer step
observations.rationale: All follow-up messages end with 'After completing the work, commit and push your changes.' The implementer is instructed by its original request that CLI handles commit/push (end_turn model). This pre-existing template issue is now exposed in the unpushable-path follow-up path. In practice the agent interprets 'commit and push' as 'complete and end_turn' given its system prompt, so no functional regression, but the instruction is misleading.

findings.title: A failed worktree enumeration is treated as proof that the worktree is safe
findings.rationale: If git status fails, the collector silently omits uncommitted paths. Layer 2 then stages, commits, and pushes an undetected workflow change, reaching the remote rejection this preflight should prevent.

findings.title: Pre-commit round backstop failures whitelist the previous HEAD as a synthesized round commit
findings.rationale: When commitScopedPaths rejects a protected path before creating a commit, the round coordinator still captures the existing HEAD and records it as a synthesized commit. This corrupts the egress authorization ledger and persists misleading guidance that a round commit was created.

findings.title: An unavailable pre-commit HEAD is still interpreted as proof that a round commit was created
findings.rationale: If the pre-commit captureHeadSha call returns null but the post-call capture succeeds after a pre-commit backstop rejection, the comparison treats the unchanged existing HEAD as newly created. That OID is appended to synthesizedCommits, weakening the egress authorization boundary. Require both HEAD observations to be non-null before inferring advancement.
